# Original response cards
R1: A permitted account exports 500 records; the user says the task was not theirs. Deletion is denied. Compare authentication, authorisation and accounting gaps; corroborate attribution and the export destination.
R2: Booking-server files are unreadable and there is a disclosure demand. A backup exists, but the last restore test is unknown. Plan verified recovery and state limits without declaring confidentiality resolved.
R3: A new IPS rule blocks a legitimate booking workflow. Disabling all rules restores access. Compare focused tuning or an exception with blanket disabling, explaining residual risk.
R4: A laptop is lost, with possible cached records and an active session. Encryption status is uncertain. Identify evidence and an authorised response rather than assuming exposure or no exposure.
All cases are fictional; analysis does not authorise account or network changes. For each, state the asset, CIA/AAA, evidence, alternatives, controls, test, limit and response.
